definition: a district that is under the religious care of a bishop

collocations.example: The diocese of Oxford covers a large rural area.
The Catholic diocese appointed a new bishop last month.

definition: the work of managing relations between countries

collocations.example: Public diplomacy helps a nation improve its international image.
The envoy conducted shuttle diplomacy between the two governments.

definition: to think that someone or something is bad or wrong

collocations.example: Many voters disapprove of the new tax plan.
Teachers strongly disapprove when students cheat on exams.

definition: to take weapons away from a person or group

collocations.example: The peacekeepers worked to disarm the warring militias.
Government troops moved in to disarm the rebel group.

definition: to see or understand something that is not obvious

collocations.example: Analyzts could discern a clear pattern in the data.
Investigators struggled to discern the truth from the testimony.

definition: a difference between two things that should be the same

collocations.example: There is a discrepancy between the two accounts.
The auditor found a statistical discrepancy in the report.

definition: the loss of respect because you have done something wrong

collocations.example: The minister resigned in disgrace after the scandal.
The scandal brought public disgrace on the whole family.

definition: to break into small pieces or fall completely apart

collocations.example: The old manuscript began to disintegrate the moment it was touched.
Cheap plastic toys often disintegrate completely within a year.

definition: to not like someone or something

collocations.example: Many customers strongly dislike the new store layout.
She seemed to dislike him intensely from the start.

definition: to take something apart into separate pieces

collocations.example: Engineers had to dismantle the machine for repairs.
Workers will dismantle the scaffolding after the repairs.

definition: a strong feeling of shock and disappointment

collocations.example: She looked at the broken vase in dismay.
To his dismay, the flight was canceled again.

definition: to give out or supply something to people

collocations.example: The pharmacist is licensed to dispense prescription medication.
This machine can dispense cash in several currencies.

definition: a person's natural character or usual mood

collocations.example: She has a cheerful disposition and smiles often.
The ride is unsuitable for people of a nervous disposition.

definition: strong disagreement with an official or widely held opinion

collocations.example: The government harshly suppressed all political dissent.
Several members voiced dissent during the meeting.

definition: a long narrow channel dug in the ground for water

collocations.example: The car skidded off the road into a drainage ditch.
Farmers dug an irrigation ditch across the dry field.

definition: to go in different directions or become different

collocations.example: Opinions diverge sharply on how to solve this.
The new road diverges from the old route here.

definition: to increase the variety of products or activities

collocations.example: The company plans to diversify its product range.
Advisers urge clients to diversify their investments widely.

definition: something that draws attention away from something else

collocations.example: The thieves created a diversion to distract the guards.
He set off the alarm as a diversion.

definition: to change the direction or purpose of something

collocations.example: The politician tried to divert attention from the scandal.
The company diverted funds to its new project.

definition: feeling as if everything is spinning and you might fall

collocations.example: Standing up too fast can make you feel dizzy.
She had a sudden dizzy spell and sat down.

definition: to avoid something by moving quickly or cleverly

collocations.example: The boxer quickly ducked to dodge the sudden punch.
She had to dodge the traffic to cross.

definition: money paid by the government to people who are unemployed

collocations.example: He has been on the dole since the factory closed.
Many graduates joined the dole queue that year.

definition: the state of being more powerful or important than others

collocations.example: The firm enjoys clear market dominance in this region.
The new champion quickly established dominance over his rivals.

definition: death, destruction, or a terrible fate that cannot be avoided

collocations.example: A feeling of impending doom slowly filled the room.
A sense of doom hung over the city.

definition: to hang or arrange cloth loosely over something

collocations.example: She draped a blanket over the sleeping child.
He draped a scarf around his neck loosely.

definition: severe and sudden in effect; extreme

collocations.example: The company took drastic measures to cut costs.
There will have to be some drastic changes.

definition: a strong feeling of fear about something that may happen

collocations.example: The thought of the exam fills me with dread.
A sense of dread came over her suddenly.

definition: extremely bad or unpleasant

collocations.example: We have made a dreadful mistake with the order.
They told us the dreadful news this morning.

definition: a long period of time with little or no rain

collocations.example: The severe drought destroyed most of the crops.
The government sent drought relief to the farmers.

definition: drunk, or caused by drinking too much alcohol

collocations.example: He was arrested for drunken driving last night.
The two men got into a drunken brawl.

definition: to replace or add a soundtrack in another language to a film

collocations.example: They will dub the film for foreign audiences.
The cartoon was dubbed into English last year.

definition: not to be trusted; of doubtful quality or honesty

collocations.example: The firm engaged in some highly dubious practices.
Her claim seemed highly dubious to the committee.

definition: stupid or silly (informal)

collocations.example: That was a really dumb idea from the start.
There is no such thing as a dumb question.

definition: an exact copy of something

collocations.example: Please keep a duplicate copy of the contract.
She had a duplicate key cut for the office.

definition: able to last a long time without being damaged

collocations.example: This fabric is strong and durable enough for daily use.
The store sells durable goods like appliances and furniture.

definition: the time in the evening when the sky begins to get dark

collocations.example: The street lights come on at dusk.
We reached the campsite just before dusk.

definition: a substance used to change the color of something

collocations.example: She used a brown hair dye to cover gray.
The fabric dye left stains on her hands.

definition: the forces or processes that cause change within a group or system

collocations.example: The manager studies group dynamics within her team.
Market dynamics can shift quickly during a crisis.

definition: serious and sincere in what you say or do

collocations.example: The earnest young doctor answered every question carefully.
She made an earnest effort to improve her grades.

definition: a sudden violent shaking of the ground

collocations.example: A major earthquake struck the coastal city overnight.
Rescue teams assessed the earthquake damage the next morning.

definition: behaving in a strange or unusual way

collocations.example: Everyone thought the eccentric old man was harmless.
Her eccentric behavior amused and puzzled the neighbors.

definition: an occasion when one object in space blocks light from another

collocations.example: A total solar eclipse will occur next spring.
We watched the lunar eclipse from the hilltop.

definition: the relationship between living things and their environment

collocations.example: Oil spills can damage the fragile ecology of reefs.
Scientists study the marine ecology of the bay.

definition: a feeling of very great happiness

collocations.example: The fans screamed in ecstasy as the band appeared.
Her face showed sheer ecstasy at the news.

definition: the ability of something to produce the result you want

collocations.example: Studies confirm the efficacy of regular exercise.
Researchers tested the clinical efficacy of the new drug.

definition: able to stretch and then return to its original shape

collocations.example: She tied her hair back with an elastic band.
These trousers have a comfortable elastic waistband.

definition: all the people who are allowed to vote in an election

collocations.example: There is widespread apathy among the electorate.
The party lost the trust of the general electorate.

definition: to get information or a reaction from someone

collocations.example: The teacher's question failed to elicit any response.
Detectives tried to elicit information from the witness.

definition: difficult to find, catch, or achieve

collocations.example: A lasting peace remains an elusive goal here.
The elusive suspect avoided the police for months.

definition: to start something new and usually difficult

collocations.example: They decided to embark on a long sea journey.
She hopes to embark on a nursing career soon.

definition: to fix something firmly into a surrounding substance

collocations.example: The surgeon had to embed the pin in the bone.
The ancient fossil was firmly embedded in the rock.

definition: to decorate cloth by sewing patterns onto it

collocations.example: She likes to embroider flowers on her cushions.
The tailor will embroider a design on the collar.

definition: an animal or human in the earliest stage before birth

collocations.example: The scientists examined a human embryo under the microscope.
Embryo research raises many difficult ethical questions.

definition: to leave your own country to live in another one

collocations.example: They decided to emigrate to Australia last year.
Many families emigrate from poorer regions each year.

definition: to give someone the power or confidence to do something

collocations.example: Good managers empower employees to make their own decisions.
Education can empower people to change their lives.

definition: to include a wide range of things

collocations.example: The new rules encompass a wide range of activities.
Her duties encompass everything from hiring to budgeting.

definition: to cut words or designs into a hard surface

collocations.example: The jeweller will engrave your name on the ring.
They chose to engrave a message on the trophy.

definition: to get someone's help or support for something

collocations.example: They hoped to enlist the help of local volunteers.
The campaign tried to enlist support from young voters.

definition: to ask someone for information

collocations.example: I called the station to enquire about train times.
She wrote to enquire whether the job was still open.

definition: a small group of musicians who perform together

collocations.example: The jazz ensemble performed at the city festival.
She plays violin in a small string ensemble.

definition: to happen after or as a result of something

collocations.example: The lights went out and total chaos ensued.
A heated debate ensued after the announcement.

definition: to involve something as a necessary part or result

collocations.example: Any investment of this kind will entail serious risks.
The job will entail working long hours each week.

definition: a substance in living things that speeds up chemical reactions

collocations.example: A digestive enzyme helps break down the food.
The drug reduces the enzyme activity in cells.

definition: a long film or book about heroic deeds and events

collocations.example: The director's new film is a three-hour Hollywood epic.
The novel is a sweeping historical epic about war.

definition: a disease that spreads quickly to many people at once

collocations.example: Doctors feared a worldwide flu epidemic that winter.
Health officials worked hard to contain the epidemic.

definition: a state of balance between opposing forces or feelings

collocations.example: The economy finally reached a state of equilibrium.
He sat quietly to recover his emotional equilibrium.

definition: to remove something completely so it cannot be seen

collocations.example: Please erase the whiteboard completely after the lesson.
You can erase pencil marks with a good eraser.

definition: to gradually wear away or destroy something

collocations.example: The waves erode the coastline a little each year.
Heavy rain can gradually erode the soil on steep slopes.

definition: the gradual wearing away of soil or rock

collocations.example: Planting trees helped reduce soil erosion on the hill.
Coastal erosion threatens many homes near the sea.

definition: to become or make something more serious or intense

collocations.example: The border dispute could escalate the tensions further.
A small argument can escalate quickly into violence.

definition: lasting forever; without end

collocations.example: Many religions promise believers eternal life after death.
She thanked them with a smile of eternal gratitude.

definition: relating to a Protestant tradition that stresses the gospel

collocations.example: She attends a large evangelical church downtown.
The evangelical preacher drew huge crowds every Sunday.

definition: to change from a liquid into a gas or vapor

collocations.example: Blowing warm air makes the water evaporate faster.
Shallow puddles evaporate quickly on a sunny day.

definition: to make a bad situation or problem worse

collocations.example: Cutting the budget will only exacerbate the problem.
His careless remarks exacerbated tensions between the groups.

definition: a wide and open area of land, water, or sky

collocations.example: The desert stretched out in a vast expanse.
Below us lay a huge expanse of water.

definition: to officially force someone to leave a place or group

collocations.example: The school may expel students for serious misconduct.
They threatened to expel him from the country.

definition: to reach the end of the period when something can be used

collocations.example: Your driving license will expire at the end of May.
The special offer will expire soon, so hurry.

definition: extremely beautiful and delicately made

collocations.example: We admired the exquisite craftsmanship of the vase.
The painting was admired for its exquisite detail.

definition: the outer surface or appearance of something

collocations.example: The exterior of the house needs fresh paint.
The new car has a smooth, aerodynamic exterior.

definition: no longer existing as a living species

collocations.example: Many species may become extinct within a century.
The dodo is a famous extinct bird species.

definition: extremely good; wonderful

collocations.example: Jane is a fabulous cook and loves entertaining.
We had a fabulous time at the beach.

definition: relating to a person's face

collocations.example: His facial expression did not change at all.
The software can recognize people by their facial features.

definition: based on facts rather than opinions or guesses

collocations.example: The report contained several serious factual errors.
Please check the factual information before publishing it.

definition: an act of saying goodbye when leaving

collocations.example: They held a farewell party for the retiring manager.
She bade farewell to all her old friends.

definition: to close or join something firmly

collocations.example: Please fasten your seatbelt before the plane departs.
He could not fasten the buttons on his coat.

definition: a feeling of extreme tiredness

collocations.example: Driver fatigue was blamed for the serious accident.
Long hours of study can cause mental fatigue.

definition: able to be done or achieved; practical

collocations.example: The engineers proposed a feasible plan for the bridge.
The project is not economically feasible right now.

definition: a large special meal for many people

collocations.example: The whole village attended the grand wedding feast.
They prepared a lavish feast for the holiday.

definition: to defend yourself against something by pushing it away

collocations.example: Healthy trees can fend off an insect attack better.
The minister struggled to fend off harsh criticism.

definition: cheerful and suitable for a celebration

collocations.example: Shops are always busy during the festive season.
The whole town was in a festive mood.

definition: a violin, especially one used for folk music (informal)

collocations.example: He learned to play the fiddle as a child.
The musician tuned his old fiddle before the dance.

definition: disgusting dirt

collocations.example: The abandoned house was covered in filth.
They spent hours cleaning the filth and grime.

definition: a piece of equipment fixed in place in a building

collocations.example: The electrician replaced the old light fixture.
They installed a new bathroom fixture last week.

definition: a small, thin, flat piece of something

collocations.example: A single flake of snow landed on her glove.
Flakes of old paint peeled off the wall.

definition: to suddenly burn more brightly or become more intense

collocations.example: The fire will flare up if you add fuel.
The flames suddenly flared as the strong wind rose.

definition: a set of rooms for living in, usually on one floor; a British apartment

collocations.example: They decided to rent a small flat near the station.
She bought a one-bedroom flat in the city.

definition: to praise someone too much, often in an insincere way

collocations.example: He always tries to flatter the boss for favors.
